rawFindings.description: The `runId` parameter was removed from `deriveSummary` but `runId` is still available in `writeTraceFile` (the only caller). The removal itself is fine, but the ADR and code comments already acknowledge that `src/trace.ts` and `dashboard/src/data/schema.ts` must be kept in sync manually with no test to catch drift. This makes the trace format a silent failure point: any future change to either side will not be caught until the dashboard renders incorrectly.
rawFindings.suggestedFix: Add a test that serialises a TraceFile via `writeTraceFile` and then parses it through the dashboard's Zod schema, so producer/consumer divergence fails CI immediately rather than silently breaking the dashboard.

rawFindings.description: The `max_tokens` truncation check and its error message both hard-code the string `MAX_TOKENS` and the constant value is referenced only by the constant itself. If `MAX_TOKENS` is ever changed, the error message text referencing `review-call.ts` will still be accurate, but the comment directing engineers to "Raise MAX_TOKENS in review-call.ts" is fragile documentation that will drift if the constant is moved or renamed.
rawFindings.suggestedFix: Interpolate the actual `MAX_TOKENS` value into the error message (e.g. `${MAX_TOKENS}-token`) so the message stays accurate without a manual update, which is already done — just remove the redundant prose reference to the file name.

events.verdictRationale: This PR touches a broad set of files across the Sentinel codebase; the two surviving findings are both maintainability concerns — a lack of cross-boundary schema drift detection between trace producer and dashboard consumer, and fragile hard-coded documentation in an error message — with no security or correctness blockers identified.
